en.title: Product of the Maximum and Minimum in a Dataset
en.description: Starting from an empty multiset, process the operations in order: `push x` inserts one x; `pop x` removes a single copy of an x that is currently present. After each operation, output the product of the current minimum and maximum of the set; if the set is empty, output 0, consistent with all three implementations in the fixed source (Python, Java, C++).
en.input: The first line contains the number of operations n, followed by n lines, each `push x` or `pop x`. Complete original constraints: 1≤n≤100000, 1≤x≤10^9; whenever a pop is executed, the current multiset contains at least one x. The ranges of the fixed complete raw are kept; the standard input/output is this site's wrapper.
en.output: On each line, output the product after the corresponding operation; output 0 when the multiset is empty. Compute the product as a 64-bit integer.
en.explanation: Duplicate values are handled as a multiset, and pop removes only one copy; this behavior matches the reference implementations in the three languages of the fixed source.
hints: Use a min-heap, a max-heap, and a frequency table; when deleting elements, use the frequency table to lazily clean up the heap tops.
